paragraphs: Rabbi Achai bar Yoshiyah, Eruvin 13a; Sotah 20b. Gittin 45a has Rabbi Achi; Nedarim 20a, Acha; Ein Yaakov, Rabbi Achi. He had silver vessels in Nehardea and told them to give them to Rabbi Dostai son of Rabbi Yannai (see there) and Rabbi Yose ben Kippur, Gittin 14a. (Mekhilta, Bo, section 3: Rabbi Yishmael says, etc.; Rabbi Achi bar Yoshiyah says, etc.; Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai says.) Rabbi spoke prophetically on the day he died. In Setya, a Babylonian town, they caught fish on Shabbat; Rabbi Achai bar Yoshiyah excommunicated them, Asarah Yuchasin 72a. This requires examination: he was in Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai’s days, yet alive at Rabbi’s death. They were digging in the ground; a man snorted at them—that is, Rabbi Achai bar Yoshiyah. Rav Nachman told him, “But the righteous will become dust!” He replied, “That is one who has envy,” Shabbat, Sho'el 152b. Tractate Kallah has Rabbi Yochai bar Yoshiyah—an error. It appears there were two Rabbi Achai bar Yoshiyahs: one in Rabbi Dostai son of Rabbi Yannai and Rabbi Yose ben Kippur’s time, before Rabbi and in Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai’s generation; the other at the end of Rabbi’s days. Rabbi Achai asked Rabbi Chiyya and recited in Rabbi Chiyya’s house. Rashi: a sage’s name. Apparently he is the son of Yoshiyah in Rabbi’s time. I saw Berakhot 14a: Achi (his name), a reciter of Rabbi Chiyya’s school (who recited in Rabbi Chiyya’s house), asked Rabbi Chiyya. Bekhorot 24, beginning of b: Rabbi Yochanan said, “Achi Berabbi asks” (Rashi: a great and distinguished man in his generation); see Berabbi.
